captured.notes: Partial capture: three of the fixture's seven matrices (the criteria matrix and the Learning and Vocational Training school matrices), chosen to cover the fixture's famously inconsistent criteria matrix and the matrix sizes where the tool's CR convention differs most visibly from the fixture's declared table. The calculator evaluates one matrix per session; it does not compose hierarchies without a login, so no synthesis is captured. Judgments entered by browser automation with per-judgment read-back; outputs transcribed verbatim; manually checked by the operator before commit. No login was used.

criteria.notes: Displayed 32.1%, 13.9%, 3.5%, 12.8%, 23.7%, 13.9%; CR '22.7%'; 'Principal eigen value = 7.420'. The tool accepted and evaluated the strongly inconsistent matrix without blocking.

ri_table.name: other
ri_table.source: Confirmed from the published source code (github.com/bpmsg/ahp-os, classes/AhpCalc.php, setAlonsoCr(), displayed by ahp-calc.php): CR = (lambda_max - n) / ((2.7699*n - 4.3513) - n), the linear fit proposed by Alonso & Lamata (2006). The values given here are the effective RI(n) = (1.7699*n - 4.3513)/(n - 1) implied by the formula at the sizes captured: 0.4793 at n = 3 (published tables: Saaty 1980 0.58, Alonso-Lamata Table 1 0.5245) and 1.2536 at n = 6 (published tables: 1.24 and 1.2479). The displayed CRs reproduce the formula directly: 22.7% (criteria), 5.6% (Learning), 21.8% (Vocational Training).

matrices.criteria.priorities.note: Matches the fixture's derived expected values at the tool's display precision (percentages to one decimal). Tolerance 0.001 because a value at a rounding boundary (13.95%) displays as 13.9.

matrices.criteria.cr.note: Displayed 0.227 vs expected 0.229011 (Saaty 1980 RI): a random-index difference - see the capture-level explanation.

explanation: All three displayed consistency ratios differ from the fixture's expected values (criteria 0.227 vs 0.229011; Learning 0.056 vs 0.046225; Vocational Training 0.218 vs 0.179714). All are random-index differences, not disagreements about the judgments or the eigenvector: the tool computes CR with the Alonso-Lamata linear fit, whose effective RI at n = 3 (0.4793) is about 17 percent below the Saaty (1980) value (0.58) the fixture declares - which is why the n = 3 divergences are large in relative terms (21 percent both) while the n = 6 divergence is under one percent. All priorities and principal eigenvalues match at display precision.

reverify.instructions: Open https://bpmsg.com/ahp/ahp-calc.php (no account needed) and run three sessions. (1) 6 criteria named as in the fixture; judgments from the fixture's criteria matrix (Learning 4 over Friends, 3 over School Life, equal to Vocational Training, 3 over College Preparation, 4 over Music Classes; Friends 7 over School Life, 3 over Vocational Training, College Preparation 5 over Friends, Friends equal to Music Classes; Vocational Training 5 over School Life, College Preparation 5 over School Life, Music Classes 6 over School Life; Vocational Training equal to College Preparation, Music Classes 3 over Vocational Training; College Preparation 3 over Music Classes). (2) 3 criteria School A/B/C with the Learning matrix (B 3 over A, C 2 over A, B 3 over C). (3) The same names with the Vocational Training matrix (A 9 over B, A 7 over C, C 5 over B). Read the priorities, CR and principal eigen value from each results page.
